optionExplanations: 统一扩容会让低吞吐 topic 也占用多余资源，颗粒度太粗。
只加 broker、不加分区，新机器依旧没有分区可接，仍然空闲。
各 topic 按自己的吞吐需求单独决定分区数：高吞吐的多给分区，低吞吐的单 broker 就够，这才是实际的扩容思路。
消费者数量应该跟着分区数走，而不是倒过来用消费者数量决定扩容规模。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling the whole cluster uniformly wastes resources on low-throughput topics too — too coarse a unit.
Just adding brokers without adding partitions leaves the new machines with nothing to pick up.
Each topic sizes its own partition count to its own throughput — heavy topics get more partitions, light ones stay on a single broker — that's the actual scaling unit.
Consumer count should follow partition count, not the other way around deciding how much to scale.

scenario: 广告点击流按 ad id 分区，Nike 投放了一支 Lebron James 爆款广告。
scenario_en: Ad clicks are partitioned by ad id, and Nike launches a viral Lebron James ad.
q: 这支爆款广告的点击流量会给系统带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem does this viral ad create for the system?
options: 所有点击涌进同一个分区，形成热分区
Kafka 会自动为它新增分区分流
点击事件会被自动均匀打散到各分区
broker 会自动对这个 key 限流
why: 同 key 同分区是把双刃剑：单个 key 流量暴涨时，它所在的分区就成了热点——面试官最爱追问这个后续问题。
why_en: All clicks for the viral ad hash to the same partition, overwhelming it with traffic and creating a hot partition.
options_en: All clicks for that ad pour into one partition, creating a hot partition.
Kafka automatically adds a new partition to spread it out.
The clicks get automatically spread evenly across partitions.
The broker automatically throttles that key.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下的一个有序、不可变、只追加写入的消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 默认使用的哈希函数，把 key 映射成分区号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Murmur2 is the default hash function Kafka uses to map a key to a partition number.

optionExplanations: partition = hash(ad_id) % N 对这一个 key 恒定不变，爆款广告的所有点击都会落进同一个分区，形成热点。
分区数是静态配置，Kafka 不会因为某个 key 变热就自动新增分区。
同 key 同分区本来就是为了保序而设计的，不会因为流量大就自动打散。
Kafka 没有针对单个热 key 的自动限流机制，需要业务自己处理。
optionExplanations_en: partition = hash(ad_id) % N stays fixed for that one key, so every click on the viral ad piles into the same partition — a hot partition.
Partition count is a static setting; Kafka doesn't add partitions automatically just because one key gets hot.
Same-key-same-partition exists specifically to preserve order — it doesn't scatter just because volume spikes.
Kafka has no built-in throttle for a single hot key; that has to be handled at the application layer.

scenario: 点击事件之间不存在顺序依赖，只求吞吐最大、分布最均匀。
scenario_en: Click events have no ordering dependency; the only goal is maximum throughput and the most even distribution.
q: 在这个前提下，最简单的热分区解法是？
q_en: Under this premise, what is the simplest hot-partition fix?
options: 加大单个分区的存储容量，热点还是集中在同一个分区上
干脆不设 key，让默认分区器（sticky 轮换）大致均匀分发
换更强性能的 broker，只是把瓶颈往后推，没解决流量集中
限制 Nike 的广告投放量，属于业务决策而非技术方案该做的取舍
why: 去掉 key 后，默认分区器会把点击长期摊到多个分区；代价是失去相关消息的顺序保证。顺序无关时，这个方案改动最少。
why_en: Dropping the key lets the default partitioner spread messages roughly evenly, at the cost of an ordering guarantee you did not need anyway.
whenOtherWins: 一旦下游要按 ad id 有序聚合，就不能裸奔无 key——得改用复合 key 或加盐。
tradeoff: 去 key 换来均匀分布 vs 保留 key 换来同实体内的顺序
options_en: Increase the storage capacity of the single partition, the hot spot still concentrates on the very same partition.
Drop the key entirely and let the default sticky-rotating partitioner spread traffic roughly evenly.
Move to a more powerful broker, just pushes the bottleneck further out without fixing the concentration.
Limit how much Nike can spend on the ad, a business call rather than a tradeoff a technical design should make.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不带 key 时的默认分区策略：先粘住一个分区批量发送，再轮换下一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sticky partitioner is the default no-key strategy that batches to one partition, then rotates.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下的一个有序、不可变、只追加写入的消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

optionExplanations: 扩容单分区容量治标不治本，热点还是集中在同一个分区上。
不带 key 时默认分区器批量轮换分区，长期看流量趋于均匀——顺序无关时这个方案改动最少。
换更强性能的 broker 只是把瓶颈往后推，没有解决流量集中的根因。
限制广告投放会直接影响业务决策，不是技术方案该做的取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Growing a single partition's capacity is a band-aid — the hot key still lands on that one partition.
Without a key, the default partitioner rotates across partitions over time, averaging out evenly — the smallest change when order doesn't matter.
A beefier broker just pushes the bottleneck further out; it doesn't fix the underlying traffic concentration.
Capping the ad's spend is a business call, not something a technical design should be making.

scenario: 还想保留一定的 key 结构，但要把爆款广告的流量摊到多个分区，能接受消费端聚合变复杂。
scenario_en: You still want a key structure, but you can accept more complex consumer aggregation to spread a viral ad across partitions.
q: 这种把热 key 拆开分摊的手法叫什么？
q_en: What is this technique for splitting a hot key across partitions called?
options: 背压（back pressure），只调发送速度，不改变 key 到分区的映射
增加副本因子（replication factor），影响的是容错，跟单 key 流量分布无关
干脆不设 key 分发，会连同一广告内部的关联信息也一起丢掉
随机加盐（salting）：ad id 拼上随机数或时间戳做分区 key
why: 加盐把一个热 key 拆成多个分区 key，负载摊开；代价是同一广告的数据散在多个分区，消费端聚合逻辑变复杂。
why_en: Salting appends a random number to the hot key to spread it across partitions, at the cost of more complex consumer-side aggregation.
whenOtherWins: 若存在天然的第二维度（地域、用户段），复合 key 比随机盐更可控、聚合也更自然。
tradeoff: 加盐换来负载分摊 vs 复合 key 换来更可控的聚合
options_en: Back pressure, only adjusts send rate, without changing the key-to-partition mapping.
Increasing the replication factor, affects fault tolerance, unrelated to one key's traffic distribution.
Dropping the key entirely, would also throw away the association info within that one ad.
Random salting: append a random number or timestamp to the ad ID to form the partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者感知到下游消费延迟变高后，主动放慢发送速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back pressure is the producer slowing down after sensing that consumer lag has grown too high.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个分区维护的副本总数，含 leader 本身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The replication factor is the total number of copies, including the leader, kept for each partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个字段拼在一起组成的分区 key，比如广告 ID + 地域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A compound key concatenates two fields, like ad ID plus region, into one partition key.

optionExplanations: 背压调的是发送速度，不改变 key 到分区的映射关系。
副本因子影响的是容错和持久性，跟单 key 流量分布无关。
干脆不设 key 会连同一广告内部的关联信息也一起丢掉，是更彻底但代价更大的方案。
把 ad id 拼上随机数或时间戳做分区 key，负载摊开——代价是消费端要把多个分区的结果合并回一个广告的总数。
optionExplanations_en: Back pressure throttles send rate; it doesn't touch the mapping from key to partition.
Replication factor affects fault tolerance and durability, unrelated to how one key's traffic distributes.
Dropping the key entirely would also throw away the related-events grouping within one ad — a more drastic option with a bigger cost.
Append a random number or timestamp to ad id as the partition key, spreading the load — the tradeoff is the consumer now has to merge results back across partitions for one ad's total.

scenario: 点击数据天然带地域属性，且地域和广告 ID 相互独立变化，想更均匀地分摊爆款广告流量。
scenario_en: Click data has a natural region attribute that varies independently from ad id, and you want to spread a viral ad more evenly.
q: 在这个前提下，最合适的 key 设计是？
q_en: Under this premise, what is the best key design?
options: 复合 key：ad id + 地域
只用消息到达时间戳做 key
只用处理该消息的 broker 编号
只用消息体的字节大小
why: 复合 key 用一个独立变化的属性把热 key 拆开：同一广告不同地域进不同分区，同地域内仍保序。
why_en: A compound key like ad ID plus region spreads the hot ad across partitions using an attribute that varies independently.
whenOtherWins: 找不到与热 key 独立变化的属性时，随机加盐是退而求其次的选择。
tradeoff: 复合 key 换来可控的分摊+局部有序 vs 随机加盐换来更均匀但聚合更零散
options_en: A compound key: ad ID plus region.
Just use the message arrival timestamp as the key.
Just the broker number that happens to handle it.
Just the byte size of the message body.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个字段拼在一起组成的分区 key，比如广告 ID + 地域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A compound key concatenates two fields, like ad ID plus region, into one partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下的一个有序、不可变、只追加写入的消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

optionExplanations: 把 ad id 和地域组合成 key，同一广告按地域分流、同一地域内部仍保序，聚合口径也清晰。
同一时刻大量点击可能共享同一时间戳，反而无法有效分摊。
broker 编号是路由的结果而不是原因，不能拿来当分区 key 的业务属性。
消息大小跟业务实体毫无关联，反映不出需要分摊的维度。
optionExplanations_en: Combine ad id with region as the key: the same ad fans out by region while staying ordered within each region, keeping aggregation clean.
A lot of clicks can share the exact same timestamp at once, so it fails to actually spread anything.
Broker number is the result of routing, not a business attribute you can use as a partitioning key.
Message size has nothing to do with the business entity, so it doesn't reflect the dimension you actually need to spread.

scenario: 允许牺牲一点实时性，希望用最省事的方式防止热分区被打爆。
scenario_en: You can trade a little freshness for the easiest way to keep a hot partition from being overwhelmed.
q: 「背压（back pressure）」方案具体是怎么做的？
q_en: How does the back-pressure approach work here?
options: 直接丢弃超出容量的消息，意味着数据永久丢失，不符合可靠性要求
把热分区手动迁到更大的机器上，但同一个 key 依旧是那个热 key，治标不治本
生产者检查分区的消费延迟（lag），太高就主动放慢发送；托管服务往往有内置机制
把消息转发到备用集群，会引入额外的一致性和路由复杂度
why: 背压 = 让生产者感知下游压力并降速，简单直接；代价是数据进入系统变慢。
why_en: Back pressure has the producer watch partition lag and slow down when it grows too high, a simple fix if you can tolerate the delay.
whenOtherWins: 实时性是硬要求时不能靠降速——去 key、加盐或复合 key 才是正解。
tradeoff: 背压换来简单省事的降速 vs 加盐/复合 key 换来不牺牲实时性的分摊
options_en: Drop messages that exceed capacity outright, meaning permanent data loss, which violates the reliability bar.
Manually move the hot partition to a bigger machine, but the same key stays the same hot key.
The producer checks partition lag and proactively slows down when it gets too high; managed services often build this in.
Forward the messages to a standby cluster, introduces extra consistency and routing complexity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者感知到下游消费延迟变高后，主动放慢发送速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back pressure is the producer slowing down after sensing that consumer lag has grown too high.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者当前 offset 和分区最新 offset 之间的差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lag is the gap between a consumer's current offset and the partition's latest offset.

optionExplanations: 丢消息意味着数据永久丢失，不符合大多数场景的可靠性要求。
换大机器只是抬高上限,同一个 key 还是全打到一个分区,热点没消除。
生产者持续检查消费延迟（lag），超过阈值就主动放慢发送，托管服务往往内置这个机制。
转发到备用集群会引入额外的一致性和路由复杂度，成本远高于简单降速。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping messages means permanent data loss, which doesn't meet most reliability requirements.
A bigger machine just raises the ceiling; the same key still lands on one partition, so the hotspot remains.
The producer keeps checking consumer lag and slows down once it crosses a threshold — managed services often build this in already.
Rerouting to a standby cluster brings in extra consistency and routing complexity, costing far more than simply slowing down.

q: 把「热分区应对」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the hot-partition response chain in the right order:
steps: 缓解：无 key / 随机加盐 / 复合 key / 背压，按顺序要求选择
现象：爆款广告使单个分区流量激增
代价：失去顺序保证，或消费端聚合逻辑变复杂
原因：partition = hash(key) % N，同一个热 key 永远打进同一分区
why: 现象→原因→缓解→代价：先解释哈希分区为什么造成热点，再给出方案并说清新引入的成本。
why_en: Name the hot partition, explain that hashing pins a hot key to one partition, offer no-key, salting, a compound key, or back pressure, then state the ordering or aggregation cost.
diagram:
flowchart TD

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个字段拼在一起组成的分区 key，比如广告 ID + 地域。

scenario: 生产者发送消息时把 acks 参数设成了 all，你要说清这具体等待了什么。
scenario_en: The producer sends messages with acks set to all, and you need to explain what it waits for.
q: acks=all 的含义是？
q_en: What does acks=all mean?
options: 等所有消费者都确认收到才算成功，跟生产者到副本之间的确认机制无关
所有 in-sync replicas（ISR）都收到，生产者才收到确认
leader 一收到就立刻确认，follower 还没同步完就可能已经丢了数据
不需要任何确认，发出去就算完，吞吐最高但完全不管数据是否真的送达
why: acks=all 让确认等到全部 ISR 落地，即便 leader 随后立刻挂掉消息也不丢——这是 Kafka 能提供的最强持久性设置。
why_en: With acks set to all, the producer is acknowledged only after every in-sync replica has the message, the strongest durability guarantee available.
options_en: Wait until every consumer confirms receipt, unrelated to the producer-to-replica acknowledgment mechanism.
The producer is acknowledged only once every in-sync replica has the message.
The leader acknowledges as soon as it receives the message, data can already be lost before a follower finishes syncing.
No acknowledgment is needed at all; fire and forget, the highest throughput but with zero regard for whether data truly arrived.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者要等多少个副本确认写入才算发送成功的配置项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Acks is the producer setting for how many replicas must confirm a write before it counts as sent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跟 leader 保持完全同步的副本集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISR, in-sync replicas, are the copies fully caught up with the partition leader.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区里处理全部读写请求的那个副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The leader replica is the copy of a partition that serves all reads and writes.

optionExplanations: acks 是生产者到 broker 副本之间的确认机制，跟消费者是否收到无关。
只有当全部 in-sync replicas 都落地，生产者才收到确认——这是 Kafka 能给的最强持久性设置。
acks=1 只等 leader 写入就确认，follower 还没同步完时数据仍可能丢。
acks=0 完全不等确认，吞吐最高但完全不管消息是否真的送达。
optionExplanations_en: acks is the confirmation between producer and broker replicas — it has nothing to do with whether a consumer received anything.
Confirmation only comes back once every in-sync replica has the message — Kafka's strongest durability setting.
acks=1 confirms as soon as the leader writes it; if followers haven't caught up yet, that data can still be lost.
acks=0 waits for no confirmation at all — highest throughput, but no guarantee the message ever actually arrived.

q: 补全常见的复制配置：
q_en: Fill in the common replication setup:
text: 复制因子（replication factor）为 {{3}} 是常见配置：每个分区共 3 个副本 = {{1}} 个 leader + {{2}} 个 follower；一台 broker 挂掉，数据仍在另外两台上。
why: RF=3 是耐用性和成本的常见平衡点：单 broker 故障后仍有两份数据，可以立刻提升一个 follower 顶上。
why_en: A replication factor of three means one leader plus two followers, so data survives a single broker failure and a follower can be promoted right away.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The replication factor is the total number of copies, including the leader, kept for each partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区里处理全部读写请求的那个副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The leader replica is the copy of a partition that serves all reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被动从 leader 同步数据、随时准备接管的副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follower replica passively copies the leader's data and stands ready to take over.

scenario: 面试官抛出一个略显不现实的问题：「如果整个 Kafka 集群都挂了怎么办」。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks the somewhat unrealistic question, what if the entire Kafka cluster goes down?
q: 面对「Kafka 整个挂了怎么办」这个问题，合理的回应是？
q_en: How should you respond to the question, what if all of Kafka goes down?
options: 立刻开始详细设计 Kafka 的灾备集群，会挤占更值得讨论的消费者故障话题
承认系统必然会彻底瘫痪，这个断言过于绝对也不准确
点出「Kafka 永远可用、偶尔一致」，把话题引向更现实的消费者故障
建议改用数据库轮询代替 Kafka，轮询数据库拿不到分区并行和保序能力
why: 行话是「Kafka 永远可用、偶尔一致」；比整个 Kafka 挂掉更值得设计的是消费者挂掉时的 offset 与再均衡处理。
why_en: Kafka is usually treated as always available and sometimes consistent, so it is worth gently steering the discussion toward the far more realistic consumer failure.
options_en: Immediately start designing a detailed Kafka disaster-recovery cluster, crowding out the far more worthwhile consumer-failure discussion.
Concede that the system will inevitably be completely down, too absolute and inaccurate a claim to make.
Note that Kafka is 'always available, sometimes consistent,' and steer toward the more realistic consumer failure.
Suggest replacing Kafka with database polling, database polling cannot match partitioned parallelism or ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

optionExplanations: 花大量时间设计一个概率极低的场景，会挤占更值得讨论的消费者故障话题。
『必然瘫痪』是过于绝对的断言，Kafka 的复制设计正是为了避免这种单点前提。
用这句话快速承认边界，再把讨论拉回 offset 提交、rebalance 这些常见故障链条。
轮询数据库拿不到 Kafka 的分区并行和保序能力，是不对等的降级替代。
optionExplanations_en: Spending a lot of time designing a near-zero-probability scenario would crowd out the more useful discussion of consumer failure.
'Inevitable total failure' is too absolute a claim — Kafka's replication design exists specifically to avoid that single point of failure.
Use that line to acknowledge the boundary quickly, then move back to common failure chains like offset commits and rebalances.
Polling a database can't match Kafka's partition parallelism and ordering guarantees — not an equivalent substitute.

scenario: 消费组里的某个消费者进程崩溃了，它原本负责的几个分区暂时没人处理。
scenario_en: One consumer process in a consumer group crashes, leaving its assigned partitions temporarily unprocessed.
q: Kafka 如何保证这些分区继续被处理？
q_en: How does Kafka make sure these partitions keep getting processed?
options: 那些分区就地暂停，直到挂掉的消费者重新上线，会拖慢整个 topic 的处理进度
消息被重定向到 DLQ，DLQ 处理的是单条消息失败而非进程失联
生产者接管消费工作，生产者和消费者的职责完全独立
触发再均衡（rebalancing）：把它的分区重新分配给组内剩余的消费者
why: 消费者挂掉后组内触发 rebalance，孤儿分区被其他成员接管，所有分区继续有人处理。
why_en: Kafka rebalances the failed consumer's partitions across the remaining group members so every partition keeps being processed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Consumer dies"] --> B["Group rebalance"]
  B --> C["Partitions reassigned"]
  C --> D["Resume from offsets"]
options_en: Those partitions pause in place until the dead consumer comes back, stalling the whole topic.
The messages get redirected to a DLQ, a DLQ handles one failed message, not an entire process going dark.
The producer takes over consumption, producer and consumer duties are entirely independent.
A rebalance is triggered: its partitions get reassigned to the remaining group members.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组成员变化时，把分区重新分配给组内消费者的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rebalancing reassigns partitions among a consumer group's members whenever membership changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享同一个 groupId、共同分摊某 topic 全部分区的消费者集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing one groupId that split up a topic's partitions.

optionExplanations: 分区不会干等:组内会 rebalance 让其他消费者立刻接管,不必等它复活。
DLQ 处理的是单条消息失败，不是消费者进程整体失联，这是两类不同的问题。
生产者和消费者是完全独立的两端，生产者不会代替消费者干活。
触发再均衡：组内存活的消费者分摊接手孤儿分区，从各自最后提交的 offset 继续处理。
optionExplanations_en: Partitions don't just wait: the group rebalances so others take over immediately, no need for it to return.
A DLQ handles single-message failures, not an entire consumer process going missing — two different problems.
Producers and consumers are fully independent roles; a producer never takes over consuming.
A rebalance fires: the surviving consumers in the group split up the orphaned partitions and pick up from their last committed offsets.

scenario: 一个消费者进程崩溃后重启，它需要知道自己该从哪里接着读。
scenario_en: After a consumer process crashes and restarts, it needs to know where to resume reading.
q: 重启后的消费者从哪里继续读消息？
q_en: Where does a restarted consumer continue reading from?
options: 从分区最开头重新读一遍，会造成大量不必要的重复处理
从自己最后提交（committed）的 offset 继续
从最新写入的消息开始读，会跳过重启期间尚未处理完的部分
从一个随机位置开始读，忽略了进度其实是被持久化记录的
why: 提交 offset 就是消费者对 Kafka 说「这条我处理完了」；重启后读回最后提交点继续，不漏消息（但可能重复）。
why_en: A restarted consumer reads its last committed offset from Kafka and resumes from there, missing nothing though possibly reprocessing a message.
options_en: Re-read the entire partition from the beginning, causing a large amount of unnecessary duplicate processing.
Resume from its own last committed offset.
Start reading from the newest message, would skip whatever was left unprocessed during the outage.
Start from a random position, ignoring that progress is in fact durably recorded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息在分区内的顺序位置编号，消费者用它记录读到哪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a message's sequential position within its partition, used to track consumer progress.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享同一个 groupId、共同分摊某 topic 全部分区的消费者集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing one groupId that split up a topic's partitions.

optionExplanations: 从头重读会造成大量不必要的重复处理，且丢掉了已提交进度这个信息。
重启后读回自己最后提交的 offset 继续——这正是提交 offset 的意义所在。
只读最新消息会跳过重启期间尚未处理完的部分，造成漏处理。
消费进度是被持久化记录在 Kafka 内部特殊 topic 里的，不存在随机起点。
optionExplanations_en: Re-reading from the start causes a mountain of needless reprocessing and throws away the progress already committed.
It resumes from its own last committed offset — that's the entire point of committing in the first place.
Reading only the newest messages would skip whatever was left unprocessed when it crashed, causing gaps.
Progress is durably recorded in one of Kafka's internal topics keyed by consumer group — there's no random starting point.

scenario: 网页爬虫：消费者取到 URL、下载 HTML、存入 blob 存储。要保证 HTML 绝不丢。
scenario_en: A web crawler consumer fetches a URL, downloads HTML, and writes it to blob storage; the HTML must not be lost.
q: 这个场景下，offset 应该什么时候提交？
q_en: In this scenario, when should the offset be committed?
options: 确认 HTML 已成功写入 blob 存储之后再提交
刚取到消息就立刻提交，等于在工作完成前就许下承诺
刚开始下载时就提交，下载随时可能失败或崩溃在中途
定时无条件提交，不管处理到哪一步，可能提交到还没处理完的位置
why: 提交 = 宣布这条不再重来；在结果真正持久化之前提交，崩溃就等于丢活。晚提交换来的重复处理用幂等消化。
why_en: Commit the offset only after the HTML is safely stored, since committing any earlier means a crash would silently lose that work.
whenOtherWins: 如果重复处理的代价高于丢一条的代价（比如会重复扣款），就要反过来早提交甚至用事务性输出。
tradeoff: 晚提交防止丢工作 vs 早提交避免重复处理
options_en: Commit only after the HTML is confirmed written to blob storage.
Commit the instant the message is fetched, effectively promising completion before the work is even done.
Commit as soon as the download starts, the download can still fail or crash midway through.
Commit on a timer regardless of how far processing has gotten, risks committing past a point that has not actually finished.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息在分区内的顺序位置编号，消费者用它记录读到哪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a message's sequential position within its partition, used to track consumer progress.

optionExplanations: HTML 已经安全落盘后再提交，即使这时崩溃，工作成果也不会丢。
取到消息就立刻提交等于在工作完成前先许下承诺，一旦下载或存储失败进程崩溃，这条 URL 就永远不会被重试。
下载过程随时可能失败或崩溃在中途，过早提交同样会丢工作成果。
定时无条件提交可能提交到还没处理完的位置，一样有丢工作的风险。
optionExplanations_en: Commit only after the HTML is safely written to blob storage — even a crash right then doesn't lose the work already done.
Committing the instant the message is fetched makes a promise before the work is done; if the download or write then fails and the process crashes, that URL is gone for good.
The download can fail or crash mid-way at any point, so committing that early risks losing the work just the same.
Committing on a timer regardless of progress can land on a position that hasn't actually finished processing — same risk of losing work.

scenario: 网页爬虫的消费者一次要完成下载 HTML、解析、写数据库三件事才提交 offset。
scenario_en: One crawler consumer must download HTML, parse it, write the database, and only then commit the offset.
q: 消费者单次处理的工作量太大，会带来什么风险？怎么设计能缓解？
q_en: What risk comes from making one consumer do too much work, and what design reduces it?
options: Kafka 会直接拒绝给它分配分区，分区分配只看消费组成员数量
工作量大小对系统没有实际影响，忽略了崩溃发生在中途的概率会变高
失败时要重做的工作更多——把消费者的活拆成小步骤
offset 数值会因此溢出，offset 只是一个普通的递增整数
why: 工作单元越大，崩溃后重做的浪费越大；把流水线拆成多个小步骤（每步一个 topic）能缩小重试半径。
why_en: The more work a consumer does per message, the more gets redone on failure, so keep each consumer step small, like splitting crawling into separate download and parse phases.
options_en: Kafka simply refuses to assign it any partitions, partition assignment only looks at group membership count.
The amount of work per message has no real effect on the system, ignoring that the odds of crashing midway climb higher.
More work gets redone on failure, so split the consumer's job into smaller steps.
The offset numeric value overflows because of it, the offset is really just an ordinary increasing integer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从 Kafka topic 拉取并处理消息的客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer is the client that pulls and processes messages from a Kafka topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者写入、消费者订阅的消息逻辑分类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A topic is the logical category that producers publish to and consumers subscribe from.

optionExplanations: Kafka 只按消费组成员数量分配分区，不会因为某个消费者干的活多就拒绝分配。
步骤越多，崩溃发生在中途的概率越高，重做的成本自然更大，工作量大小并非无关紧要。
工作量越大，失败要重做的越多——把爬虫拆成『下载』『解析』两个独立阶段能缩小重试半径。
offset 只是一个普通递增整数，跟单条消息处理耗时或步骤数完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka only assigns partitions based on group membership count — it never rejects assignment based on how much work a consumer does.
More steps mean a higher chance of crashing mid-way, so the redo cost is very much affected by unit size, not irrelevant.
The bigger the unit of work, the more gets redone on failure — splitting the crawler into separate 'download' and 'parse' stages shrinks the retry blast radius.
Offset is just a plain increasing integer, unrelated to how long a message takes to process or how many steps it involves.

scenario: 生产者配置了自动重试（retries: 5），但没有额外配置幂等模式。
scenario_en: The producer has automatic retries configured, but idempotence has not been configured.
q: 开启生产者自动重试时必须同时注意什么，才能不引入新问题？
q_en: What must you also consider when enabling producer retries?
options: 必须同时关闭消息压缩，压缩只影响消息大小，跟重复无关
必须开启幂等生产者（idempotent）模式
必须把 acks 设为 0，acks=0 反而让重试判断更不可靠
必须相应减小分区数，分区数决定的是并行度而非重试安全
why: 网络抖动下生产者可能把已成功的发送误判为失败而重发；幂等模式保证这类重试不产生重复消息。
why_en: Enable idempotent producer mode so a retry after a falsely presumed failure does not create a duplicate message.
options_en: You must also turn off message compression, compression only affects size, unrelated to duplicates.
You must also turn on idempotent producer mode.
You must set acks to 0, acks=0 actually makes the retry decision even less reliable.
You must correspondingly reduce the partition count, partition count governs parallelism, not retry safety.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开启后，重复发送同一条消息不会造成重复写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent producer ensures retried sends of the same message never create duplicates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者要等多少个副本确认写入才算发送成功的配置项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Acks is the producer setting for how many replicas must confirm a write before it counts as sent.

optionExplanations: 压缩只影响消息大小，跟重试是否产生重复消息无关。
必须开启幂等生产者模式：broker 靠生产者 ID 和序号识别重复发送并去重，避免『以为没发出去』的重试造成重复消息。
acks=0 完全不等确认，重试判断反而更不可靠，方向反了。
分区数决定的是并行度，跟单个生产者的重试安全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Compression only affects message size, unrelated to whether retries produce duplicates.
You need idempotent-producer mode: the broker recognizes duplicate sends by producer ID and sequence number and dedupes them, preventing a 'thought it failed' retry from creating a duplicate message.
acks=0 waits for no confirmation at all, which makes retry decisions even less reliable — the opposite direction from what's needed.
Partition count decides parallelism, unrelated to a single producer's retry safety.

scenario: 消费者处理一条消息失败了，你想知道 Kafka 本身能不能帮你自动重试。
scenario_en: A consumer fails while handling a message, and you want to know whether Kafka retries that work for you.
q: 消费端处理失败的重试，Kafka 的原生支持情况是？
q_en: What native support does Kafka provide for retrying failed consumer processing?
options: 内建指数退避重试，开箱即用，这其实是托管队列服务才有的能力
失败消息自动进 DLQ，忽略了 DLQ 是重试耗尽后的终点
不内建消费者重试，需自建 retry topic 处理失败消息
自动跳过失败消息继续往下读，Kafka 不会替你做这种取舍判断
why: Kafka 不替你做消费重试：把失败消息移到自定义 retry topic 反复处理，既能无限重试又不阻塞主消费。
why_en: Kafka has no built-in consumer retries, so the common pattern is a custom retry topic processed by a separate consumer.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    T[主 topic] --> C[消费者]
    C -- 处理失败 --> R[重试 topic]
    R --> RC[重试消费者]
    RC -- 重试次数超限 --> D[(DLQ 死信队列)]
    RC -- 成功 --> OK[完成]
options_en: Built-in exponential-backoff retries, ready out of the box, a capability that actually belongs to managed queue services.
Failed messages automatically land in a DLQ, ignoring that a DLQ is the endpoint only after retries are exhausted.
No built-in consumer retries; the common pattern is a custom retry topic for failed messages.
Automatically skip the failed message and keep reading, a call Kafka never makes on your behalf.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管消息队列服务，内置重试计数和死信队列联动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed queue with built-in retry counting and dead-letter-queue support.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存放处理失败消息、供独立消费者重试的自定义 topic。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retry topic is a custom topic that holds failed messages for a separate consumer to retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存放反复重试仍失败消息的队列，供事后排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DLQ, dead letter queue, stores messages that failed too many retries so they can be investigated later.

optionExplanations: 内建指数退避重试是 SQS 等托管队列服务的能力，不是 Kafka 原生具备的。
DLQ 是重试次数用尽后的终点，不是失败后立刻发生的第一步，这个说法搞反了流程顺序。
Kafka 不内建消费重试：常见做法是自建一个重试 topic，让独立消费者反复处理失败消息，不阻塞主消费。
Kafka 不会替你判断该不该跳过失败消息，不存在这种自动静默跳过的行为。
optionExplanations_en: Built-in exponential-backoff retry is a managed-queue feature like SQS's, not something Kafka has natively.
A DLQ is where a message lands after retries are exhausted, not the first thing that happens on failure — this mixes up the order of events.
Kafka doesn't retry consumption natively — the common pattern is a self-built retry topic that an independent consumer works through, without blocking the main flow.
Kafka never silently skips a failed message for you — that call is left entirely to the application.

scenario: 一条消息在重试 topic 里被反复处理，始终失败，重试次数已经用尽。
scenario_en: A message keeps failing in the retry topic, and its retry count has been exhausted.
q: 死信队列（DLQ）在这里的用途是？
q_en: What is the dead-letter queue used for here?
options: 存放重试多次仍失败的消息，供事后排查
专门用来加速失败消息的重新投递
把旧消息压缩归档以节省磁盘空间
给整个 topic 的所有消息做一份完整备份
why: 重试次数超限的消息移入 DLQ，不再阻塞主流程，同时保留现场供人工调查。
why_en: A dead letter queue stores messages that failed too many retries so they can be investigated later without blocking the main flow.
options_en: Store messages that failed too many retries, for later investigation.
A place used to speed up redelivery of failed messages.
Compresses and archives old messages to save disk space.
Keeps a full backup of every message in the topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存放反复重试仍失败消息的队列，供事后排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DLQ, dead letter queue, stores messages that failed too many retries so they can be investigated later.

optionExplanations: DLQ 存放重试多次仍失败的消息，带着失败上下文，方便事后人工排查。
DLQ 是隔离失败消息,不是加速重投;重投逻辑在主流程里。
压缩省空间是保留策略的事,DLQ 关心的是失败消息的去向。
备份靠副本机制,DLQ 只收留反复失败的少量消息,不是全量备份。
optionExplanations_en: The DLQ holds messages that failed even after repeated retries, keeping the failure context around for later investigation.
A DLQ isolates failed messages, it doesn't speed up redelivery, which lives in the main flow.
Saving space via compression is retention's job; a DLQ is about where failed messages go.
Backups come from replication; a DLQ only holds the few repeatedly-failed messages, not everything.

scenario: 设计网页爬虫，需要对失败 URL 反复重试并自动落入死信队列，团队不想自己实现这些机制。
scenario_en: A web crawler needs failed URLs retried and then automatically sent to a DLQ, and the team does not want to build that logic.

options: Kafka：重试计数和 DLQ 都得自建，运维全落到自己头上
Redis Pub/Sub
直接轮询数据库表
AWS SQS：重试计数和 DLQ 都是开箱即用
why: SQS 自带重试计数和 DLQ 联动，正因如此 Web Crawler 的推荐方案选了 SQS 而不是 Kafka。

tradeoff: SQS 换来内置重试/DLQ 的省事 vs Kafka 换来分区有序和多组重放的能力
options_en: Kafka: you build retry counting and the DLQ yourself, and own all the operations.
Redis Pub/Sub.
Poll a database table directly.
AWS SQS: retry counting and DLQ support are built in.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管消息队列服务，内置重试计数和死信队列联动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed queue with built-in retry counting and dead-letter-queue support.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存放反复重试仍失败消息的队列，供事后排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DLQ, dead letter queue, stores messages that failed too many retries so they can be investigated later.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

optionExplanations: Kafka 没有内置重试/DLQ,得自己搭重试 topic,省事这条上输给 SQS。
Redis Pub/Sub 没有持久化和重试语义，消息一旦没人在线就直接丢，不满足需求。
轮询数据库意味着自己实现整套重试、幂等和调度逻辑，工作量比二者都大。
SQS 原生支持每条消息的重试计数，超限自动转入 DLQ，正好满足『不想自己实现』的约束。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka has no built-in retries/DLQ; you build a retry topic yourself, so it's more work than SQS.
Redis Pub/Sub has no persistence or retry semantics — a message is gone the moment nobody's listening, which doesn't meet the requirement.
Polling a database table means implementing the whole retry, idempotency, and scheduling stack yourself — even more work than either option above.
SQS natively tracks per-message retry counts and auto-routes to a DLQ once they're exhausted — exactly matching the 'don't want to build this' constraint.

scenario: 生产者（用 KafkaJS 客户端）要连续发送三条消息，你在纠结是三次单独 send() 还是合成一次调用。
scenario_en: A producer using the KafkaJS client needs to send three messages in a row, and you are choosing between three sends and one batched call.
q: 提升 Kafka 生产端吞吐的第一个常规手段是？
q_en: What is the first common way to improve Kafka producer throughput?
options: 每条消息都单独 send() 并等它返回再发下一条，让每条消息各自承担一次完整的网络往返
批量发送：一次 send() 携带多条消息（其他客户端里等价于调大 batch.size / linger.ms 让 producer 攒批）
增加消费者数量，加消费者并不会让生产端发送更快
把消息格式改成 XML，格式更冗长通常会拖慢而非提升吞吐
why: 批量把多条消息装进一个 produce request，摊薄的是每次请求的网络往返、请求头和 broker 处理开销，还能让压缩更有效。KafkaJS 里是一次 send() 传 messages 数组；Java 客户端则由 batch.size / linger.ms 在后台按 partition 攒批。
why_en: Batching packs many messages into one produce request, spreading per-request round-trip, header and broker-side costs, and making compression more effective. In KafkaJS you pass a messages array to one send(); the Java client batches per partition in the background according to batch.size and linger.ms.
options_en: Call send() per message and await each before the next, making each message pay a full network round-trip.
Batch sends: one send() call carrying multiple messages (in other clients, the equivalent is tuning batch.size / linger.ms so the producer batches).
Add more consumers; adding consumers does not make the producer send any faster.
Switch the message format to XML; a more verbose format usually slows throughput rather than raising it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

optionExplanations: 逐条 send 每条都吃一次网络往返,吞吐最差;批量才是提吞吐的第一步。
批量把多条消息装进一个 produce request，摊薄每次请求的网络往返、请求头和 broker 处理开销，还能让压缩更有效。
生产端吞吐由生产者和 broker 决定，加消费者不会让发送更快。
XML 比常见的 JSON/二进制格式更冗长，通常会拖慢而不是提升吞吐。
optionExplanations_en: Per-message send pays a round-trip each time, the worst for throughput; batching is the first step up.
Batching packs many messages into one produce request, spreading per-request round-trip, header and broker-side costs, and making compression more effective.
Producer-side throughput is decided by the producer and broker; adding consumers doesn't make sending any faster.
XML is more verbose than the usual JSON or binary formats, so it typically hurts rather than helps throughput.

scenario: 生产者发送的都是文本类事件，你想靠压缩再省一点网络带宽。
scenario_en: The producer sends text-like events, and you want to save network bandwidth with compression.
q: Kafka 支持哪些消息压缩算法，压缩到底省的是什么？
q_en: Which compression algorithms does Kafka support, and what does compression save?
options: 只支持 ZIP 格式，这不是 Kafka 客户端里的标准选项
只支持 GZIP 一种，把可选项之一误当成唯一支持的算法
GZIP、Snappy、LZ4 等多种算法——本质是用一点 CPU 换消息变小、传得更快
Kafka 根本不支持任何压缩，这跟 producer 配置里明确存在的 compression 选项相矛盾
why: 压缩用一点 CPU 换网络带宽：消息更小、吞吐更高，对文本类载荷尤其划算。
why_en: Kafka supports algorithms like GZIP, Snappy, and LZ4, trading a bit of CPU for smaller messages that transfer faster.
options_en: Only ZIP is supported, not a standard option in Kafka client configuration.
Only GZIP is supported, wrongly treats one option among several as the only one supported.
Multiple algorithms like GZIP, Snappy, and LZ4 — trading a bit of CPU for smaller, faster-to-send messages.
Kafka supports no compression at all, contradicting the compression option that clearly exists in producer config.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

optionExplanations: ZIP 不是 Kafka 客户端配置里的标准压缩选项。
GZIP 只是可选项之一，并不是唯一支持的算法。
支持 GZIP、Snappy、LZ4 等多种算法，本质是用一点 CPU 换消息变小、传得更快，对文本类载荷尤其划算。
producer 配置里就有 compression.type,说不支持压缩与事实矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: ZIP isn't one of the standard compression options in Kafka's client config.
GZIP is just one option among several, not the only algorithm supported.
Kafka supports GZIP, Snappy, LZ4, and more — trading a bit of CPU for smaller, faster-moving messages, which pays off especially well for text-heavy payloads.
The producer config has compression.type, so claiming no compression contradicts reality.

scenario: 面试官问你，如果只能优化 Kafka 性能里的一件事，你会先从哪里下手。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks where you would start if you could optimize only one part of Kafka performance.
q: 对 Kafka 性能影响最大的单一决策是？
q_en: What single decision has the biggest impact on Kafka performance?
options: 分区 key 的选择：决定分布是否均匀、并行度上限
压缩算法的选择，省的是带宽，补不回分区不均的损失
客户端使用的编程语言，客户端语言带来的开销远小于分区策略
消息字段的命名规范，只影响可读性，不触及并行处理能力
why: 批量、压缩都是锦上添花；决定并行度和均衡度的分区策略才是性能的根，也是面试讨论的主线。
why_en: The partition key choice dominates performance because it determines parallelism and load balance, so it should be where the interview discussion starts.
options_en: The choice of partition key: it decides how evenly messages spread and caps parallelism.
The choice of compression algorithm, saves bandwidth but cannot recover the loss from uneven partitioning.
The programming language of the client, the overhead from client language choice is far smaller than partition strategy.
Naming conventions for message fields, only affects readability, never touches parallel-processing capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下的一个有序、不可变、只追加写入的消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

optionExplanations: key 选不好会出热分区，再多的批量和压缩优化都补不回并行度的损失——这是性能讨论真正该从哪里开始。
压缩能省网络带宽，但省不回分区不均带来的并行度浪费，量级远小于分区策略。
客户端语言差异带来的开销远小于分区策略的影响，不是决定性因素。
字段命名只影响可读性和序列化大小，不触及并行处理能力。
optionExplanations_en: A poorly chosen key produces a hot partition, and no amount of batching or compression can buy back the lost parallelism — that's why this is where the discussion should start.
Compression saves network bandwidth, but it can't make up for the parallelism lost to an unbalanced partition — a much smaller factor than partitioning strategy.
Differences between client languages cost far less than partitioning strategy does — not the deciding factor.
Field naming only affects readability and serialized size — it doesn't touch parallel processing at all.

scenario: 你设计的系统只需要支持「最近 3 天内」补处理失败的消费者重放，没人告诉你要改过默认配置。
scenario_en: Your system only needs to replay failed consumer work from the last three days, and nobody changed the default retention config.
q: 面试要点：不特意配置的话，Kafka 会把消息留存多长时间，这对你的重放窗口设计意味着什么？
q_en: By default, how long does Kafka retain messages, and what does that mean for your replay window?
options: 偏短：1 小时，比你需要的重放窗口短得多，必须显式调大
仍偏短：24 小时，同样短于 3 天的需求，仍需调整 retention.ms
默认恰好够用：7 天，已经覆盖你 3 天的重放需求，不用改配置
误判成永久：以为默认不清理，其实并非无限，需要主动设上限控制存储成本
why: 这是一个默认配置值，不是算出来的：默认保留 7 天，已经盖住了 3 天的重放需求；如果需求变成 30 天，才需要显式调大 retention.ms 并承担更高的存储成本。
why_en: This is a default setting, not a computed number: the default seven-day retention already covers a three-day replay need, and only a longer requirement would force you to raise retention.ms at extra storage cost.
options_en: Too short: 1 hour, far shorter than your replay window, must be explicitly increased.
Still too short: 24 hours, still shorter than the 3-day need, still requires adjusting retention.ms.
Default is just enough: 7 days, already covers your 3-day replay need, no config change required.
Mistakes it for forever: assumes nothing is cleaned up by default, when really it is not unlimited and must be capped explicitly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间控制消息在分区里保留多久的配置项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retention.ms is the config that controls how long messages are kept, measured in time.

optionExplanations: 1 小时会逼你马上调大 retention；它说明了设计含义，但不是 Kafka 的默认值。
24 小时仍盖不住 3 天重放窗口，把默认保留时间低估了。
7 天默认值已经覆盖 3 天需求，所以本题不用先改 retention.ms。
默认不是永久保留；想留更久也要给上限，不然磁盘成本会失控。
optionExplanations_en: One hour would force you to raise retention immediately; that design implication is right, but it is not Kafka's default.
Twenty-four hours still misses the three-day replay window and underestimates the default retention.
The seven-day default already covers a three-day replay need, so this case needs no retention.ms change first.
The default is not infinite retention; longer replay windows still need an explicit cap to control disk cost.

q: 补全保留策略的配置项：
q_en: Fill in the retention policy configuration fields:
text: 保留策略通过 {{retention.ms}}（按时间）和 {{retention.bytes}}（按大小）配置；加长保留时要权衡 {{存储成本}} 和性能。
why: 两个维度共同决定日志何时被清理；长保留支持重放，但磁盘账单和恢复时间都会涨。
why_en: Retention is configured by time with retention.ms and by size with retention.bytes, and longer retention costs more storage and slower recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间控制消息在分区里保留多久的配置项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retention.ms is the config that controls how long messages are kept, measured in time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按大小控制分区最多保留多少数据的配置项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retention.bytes is the config that caps how much data a partition keeps, measured in bytes.

scenario: 有人问开源 Apache Kafka 的 broker 会不会替你校验消息格式，或者要不要提前注册 Avro schema。
scenario_en: Someone asks whether an open-source Apache Kafka broker validates message formats or requires an Avro schema to be registered first.
q: Kafka 对消息内容本身的态度是？
q_en: How does Kafka treat message content itself?
options: broker 强制要求消息符合 JSON schema
broker 写入时自动校验 value 的字段类型
生产消息前必须先在 Kafka 里注册 Avro schema
不关心内容：把 key/value 当字节存储和供给，消息的序列化和解析是开发者的事
why: Apache Kafka broker 把消息 key/value 当不透明字节，只负责持久化和按 offset 供给；序列化格式由 producer/consumer 约定。Avro + Schema Registry 是常见实践，但 Schema Registry 是外部组件，不是 Kafka 的硬性要求；broker 端 schema 校验是 Confluent 商业版特性，不属于 Apache Kafka 本体。
why_en: An Apache Kafka broker treats key and value as opaque bytes, persisting them and serving them by offset; producers and consumers agree on serialization. Avro with a Schema Registry is a common practice, but the registry is an external component, not a Kafka requirement; broker-side schema validation is a Confluent commercial feature, not part of Apache Kafka.
options_en: The broker requires every message to match a JSON schema
The broker automatically validates the value's field types on write
You must register an Avro schema in Kafka before producing
It doesn't care about content: it stores and serves key/value as bytes, leaving serialization and parsing to the developer

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种二进制消息序列化格式，常配合 Schema Registry 管理消息结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Avro is a binary serialization format often paired with a Schema Registry to manage message structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 外部 schema 管理服务，负责保存消息格式版本并让生产者、消费者按约定校验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Schema Registry is an external service that stores schema versions and lets producers and consumers validate against them.

optionExplanations: Apache Kafka 的消息体是不透明的字节，协议层不强制任何 JSON schema。
broker 不解析 value 的内容，不做字段级类型校验（broker 端 schema 校验是 Confluent 商业版特性，不属于 Apache Kafka 本体）。
Avro + Schema Registry 是常见实践，但 Registry 是外部组件，不是 Kafka 要求先注册的硬性前提。
Kafka 只负责存储和供给字节，消息的序列化格式和解析由生产者和消费者自行约定。
optionExplanations_en: An Apache Kafka message body is opaque bytes; the protocol layer never enforces a JSON schema.
The broker never parses the value, so it does no field-level type checking (broker-side schema validation is a Confluent commercial feature, not part of Apache Kafka).
Avro with a Schema Registry is common practice, but the registry is an external component, not a hard prerequisite of Kafka.
Kafka only stores and serves bytes; producers and consumers agree on serialization format and parsing.

scenario: 用 kafkajs 发送订单事件，要求同一用户的事件全部落在同一分区、按序处理。
scenario_en: With kafkajs, you send order events and require all events for one user to land on one partition in order.
q: 下面哪种 send 写法能满足「同一用户事件按序处理」这个要求？
q_en: Which kafkajs send call preserves per-user event order?
options: messages: [{ value: JSON.stringify(order) }]（完全不带 key，落到随机分区）
messages: [{ key: randomUUID(), value: ... }]
topic 里带上 userId：topic: `orders-${userId}`
messages: [{ key: userId, value: JSON.stringify(order) }]
why: key=userId 让同一用户的消息哈希到同一分区、保住顺序；随机 key 或无 key 会把它们打散，按用户建 topic 则会造成 topic 数量爆炸。
why_en: Setting the key to the user ID hashes all of that user's events onto one partition and preserves their order.
whenOtherWins: 事件间无顺序要求时不带 key 反而分布最均匀、吞吐最好。
tradeoff: 按 userId 分区换来同用户内顺序 vs 无 key/随机 key 换来更均匀的分布
options_en: messages: [{ value: JSON.stringify(order) }] (no key at all, lands on a random partition)
messages: [{ key: randomUUID(), value: ... }]
Encode userId into the topic name: topic: `orders-${userId}`
messages: [{ key: userId, value: JSON.stringify(order) }]

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的 Node.js Kafka 客户端库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: kafkajs is a popular Node.js client library for talking to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下的一个有序、不可变、只追加写入的消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered, immutable, append-only log that a topic is split into.

optionExplanations: 不带 key 时消息轮询分散到各分区,同一用户的事件会乱序。
每条消息的 key 都是随机生成的，等价于随机分区，跟不带 key 一样无法保住顺序。
按用户开 topic 会让 topic 数量随用户数线性增长，运维和元数据开销随之失控。
key 设成 userId：同一用户恒定哈希到同一分区，分区内严格按写入顺序处理，唯一满足『按序处理』约束的写法。
optionExplanations_en: With no key, messages round-robin across partitions, so one user's events lose ordering.
A fresh random key on every message is equivalent to random partitioning — order is just as unguaranteed as having no key at all.
Keying by topic per user would make the topic count grow linearly with users, and ops/metadata overhead spirals out of control.
Setting key to userId hashes the same user consistently to the same partition, processed strictly in write order — the only option that actually satisfies 'process in order.'

scenario: 评论流要同时供「推送服务」和「统计服务」独立完整地消费，两边互不影响、各自记进度。
scenario_en: A comment stream must be fully consumed by both the push service and the stats service, independently and with separate progress.
q: kafkajs 消费者该怎么配置 groupId？
q_en: How should kafkajs consumers configure groupId?
options: 两个服务用不同 groupId，各自独立读全量
两个服务用同一个 groupId，会让两个业务瓜分同一批分区
统计服务直接读推送服务处理完的输出，会让统计服务被推送服务的故障拖累
开两个 topic，生产者各写一份，需要多维护一份写入逻辑还徒增存储
why: 不同 groupId 的消费组各自维护 offset、独立读同一份日志；同 groupId 则会互相分摊分区、每条消息只有一边能拿到。
why_en: Different group IDs make each service an independent consumer group that reads the full stream with its own offsets.
whenOtherWins: 想横向扩展同一个服务的处理能力时才用同一个 groupId 加更多实例。
tradeoff: 不同 groupId 换来两边各自完整消费 vs 同 groupId 换来同一服务内部的负载分摊
options_en: Give the two services different group IDs so each reads the full stream independently.
Give the two services the same group ID, which would split the same batch of partitions between two businesses.
Have the stats service read the push service's processed output directly, would drag the stats service down whenever the push service stumbles.
Open two topics and have the producer write to both, requires maintaining a second write path and wastes extra storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一个消费组的字符串；同 groupId 的消费者共享分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: groupId is the string identifying a consumer group; consumers sharing it split up the partitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享同一个 groupId、共同分摊某 topic 全部分区的消费者集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing one groupId that split up a topic's partitions.

optionExplanations: 两个服务各用自己的 groupId，各自独立维护 offset、互不干扰，都能读到全量评论。
同一个 groupId 会让两个业务被当成一个组的成员，分区被瓜分，谁都拿不到全量，违反了独立扇出的目标。
统计服务直接读推送服务的输出，会让统计被推送服务的故障或延迟拖累，产生不必要耦合。
开两个 topic 需要额外维护两份写入逻辑还徒增存储，Kafka 消费组自带的扇出能力已经够用。
optionExplanations_en: Each service uses its own groupId, tracking offsets independently and never interfering with each other — both get the full stream.
Sharing one groupId makes the two services count as members of the same group, so partitions get split between them and neither gets the full stream — defeats the independent fan-out goal.
Having the stats service read straight off the push service's output would let push service failures or delays drag stats down too — unnecessary coupling.
Two topics means maintaining two separate write paths and paying extra storage — Kafka's consumer-group fan-out already does this job for free.

q: 把「为什么给上传流水线加 Kafka」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for adding Kafka to an upload pipeline in the right order:
steps: 选型：Kafka 消息队列解耦上传与转码
代价：消费者崩溃时消息会被重复处理（at-least-once）
需求：转码耗时且可异步，上传高峰远快于处理速度
缓解：消费逻辑做成幂等，处理完成后才提交 offset
why: 需求（异步+削峰）→选型（队列）→代价（重复处理）→缓解（幂等+晚提交）：一条完整的队列选型叙事。
why_en: Async spiky work leads to choosing a Kafka queue, whose at-least-once redelivery is mitigated by idempotent consumers that commit offsets only after finishing.
whenOtherWins: 如果上传和转码必须同步完成，就不该加队列；用户要等转码结束再返回。
tradeoff: 异步队列换来上传低延迟和削峰 vs 同步处理换来没有重复消息的风险
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Blob event"] --> B["Kafka topic"]
  B --> C["Transcode worker"]
  B --> D["Thumbnail worker"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 默认的投递语义：消息保证不丢，但故障时可能被重复处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once means a message is never lost but may be reprocessed after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息在分区内的顺序位置编号，消费者用它记录读到哪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a message's sequential position within its partition, used to track consumer progress.

scenario: 生产环境里自己运维 Kafka 集群的扩容、打补丁、监控要花不少心思。
scenario_en: Running Kafka in production takes work for scaling, patching, and monitoring.
q: 生产环境里，很多 Kafka 扩容运维负担是靠什么消除的？
q_en: What removes much of Kafka's production scaling and operations burden?
options: 靠手写脚本迁移分区，手工操作容易出错也难以规模化

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 Kafka 服务，替你处理大部分集群运维。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSK, Managed Streaming for Kafka, is AWS's managed Kafka offering that handles most cluster operations for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方托管 Kafka 服务，和 AWS MSK 类似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Confluent Cloud is a third-party managed Kafka service, similar to AWS MSK.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache 开源分布式事件流平台，可当消息队列用，也可当流处理系统用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed event-streaming platform that works as either a message queue or a stream processor.

optionExplanations: 手写脚本迁移分区容易出错，也难以规模化，正是托管服务想替你消除的负担。
托管服务（Confluent Cloud、AWS MSK）把扩容、打补丁、故障切换这些操作性工作接管过去，但面试仍要懂底层的分区、复制概念。
扩容始终需要显式配置分区和 broker，不存在无限自动扩容的能力。
单机部署没有副本，一旦这台机器故障就直接丢数据或不可用，用可用性换运维简单不划算。
optionExplanations_en: Hand-written scripts for migrating partitions are error-prone and don't scale well — exactly the burden managed services aim to remove.

Managed services (Confluent Cloud, AWS MSK) take over most of the operational work — scaling, patching, failover — but interviews still expect you to understand the underlying partition and replication concepts.
Scaling always requires explicitly configuring partitions and brokers; there's no such thing as unlimited automatic scale-out.
A single-node deployment has no replicas, so one machine failing means data loss or downtime — trading away fault tolerance isn't worth the ops savings.
